=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
File: agents.md
Line or code reference: lines 1175-1178
Problem: The parenthetical in the "Already allowlisted" bullet states that a denied call is checked only when it is "a single command (no shell operator, newline, backtick, or `$(`)". This describes the pre-AD-4 quote-naive check. Following AD-4 (commits 0ffd19e and f0393e2), `_matching_allow_rule` uses `_shell_visible_text` so that operator characters inside quotes (or escaped with a backslash) do not prevent allow-rule matching.
Why it fails at runtime: Maintainers and automated agents reading agents.md receive inaccurate documentation indicating that commands containing quoted or escaped operators (such as `git merge -m 'a|b' origin/x`, which is explicitly supported and tested) are excluded from allow-rule matching and "Already allowlisted" reporting.
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

File: agents.md
Line or code reference: 1175-1177
Problem: The “single command” description excludes any shell operator, backtick, or `$(`, but the quote-aware matcher ignores operators inside quotes and escaped characters. It still treats backticks and `$(` inside double quotes as substitutions.
Why it fails at runtime: Readers may conclude that a denied command with a quoted or escaped operator is not checked for an existing allow rule, even though the helper can report it as “Already allowlisted.”
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
